name: Skagit River (Marblemount – Rockport)
blurb: Wide, gentle glacial river — famous for winter bald-eagle floats and an easy summer paddle.

sections.notes: Easy riffles and gravel bars. Watch for wood. No fee: NPS says there is no fee to raft the Skagit in a personal raft (Copper Creek), and USFS says no fees are required at Marblemount Boat Launch. USFS asks boaters to avoid beaching between Marblemount and Rockport bridges.

Classic eagle float. In winter eagle season paddlers are asked to launch between 11 am and noon so eagles can feed undisturbed in the morning. A 2026 AW trip report described heavy new wood between Marblemount and Rockport with ~3 portages — scout and check recent reports. The Cascade River joins just below the put-in, so flow here is higher than the gauge reads. Howard Miller Steelhead Park (Skagit County) charges a small ramp-use fee (AW; amount not verified).
